blocks.text: Alcohols dissociate only slightly in water: the equilibrium ROH(aq) <=> RO-(aq) + H+(aq) lies far to the left, so there are far more alcohol molecules than ions. Water also dissociates only slightly, H2O(l) <=> OH-(aq) + H+(aq), but gives more H+ ions than an alcohol does. So alcohols, with a lower [H+], are weaker acids than water.

Alcohols are less acidic than water because of their alkyl groups. Alkyl groups are electron-donating: they push electrons towards the oxygen (a positive inductive effect). This destabilises the alkoxide ion, the ion left when an alcohol loses H+, because it adds more electron density to the negative oxygen. The alkoxide ion is therefore more likely to take back an H+ ion and re-form the alcohol.

blocks.alt: Displayed ethanol (aq) in equilibrium with the ethoxide ion (aq) + H+ (aq). In the ethoxide ion the bonds H-C, C-C and C-O- carry arrowheads pointing towards O-. Two yellow boxes: 'position of the equilibrium lies to left', pointing at the equilibrium arrows, and 'alkyl group donates electron density towards O- which is more likely to accept H+ again to form CH3CH2OH', pointing at H+. Labels: ethanol, ethoxide ion, hydrogen ion.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed box reads 'to from CH3CH2OH'; it should read 'to form'.

Phenol, although it has an -OH group, is a weak acid, more acidic than water. One lone pair on the oxygen overlaps with the delocalised pi system of the ring, so in the phenoxide ion, C6H5O-, the negative charge is spread over the ring rather than held on the oxygen. This stabilises the phenoxide ion: with less charge density on the oxygen, H+ ions are not strongly attracted back, so phenol is more likely to lose a proton (act as an acid) than to gain one.

blocks.alt: The phenoxide ion drawn as a ring of six grey carbon atoms with five small H atoms and a red O atom. Two blue rings above and below the carbon ring form the extended pi system and reach over the O atom; a negative charge sign is near the O. Two blue lobes on the O are labelled '2 x sp2 - orbitals'; the blue rings are labelled 'extended pi - system'.
